text:
1. Johnson praises Shakespeare for having no heroes in his plays.
2. Johnson says Shakespeare's scenes are occupied only by ordinary men.
3. Johnson states his views with characteristic plainness.
4. In Johnson's view, other dramatists raised their characters above the common level of humanity.
5. In Johnson's view, other dramatists gave their characters sentiments no real person would express.
6. In Johnson's view, other dramatists gave their characters a manner of speech designed to win admiration rather than belief.
7. Johnson considers Shakespeare's refusal to elevate his characters one of his chief merits.
8. Shakespeare's characters speak as the reader would speak in the same situation and under the same pressure.
9. The words of Shakespeare's characters are drawn from ordinary life.
10. Shakespeare's characters move readers because readers recognise themselves in them.
11. Shakespeare's characters speak naturally even when the events of the play are improbable or supernatural.
12. Supernatural events such as ghosts and witches lie outside ordinary experience.
13. The speech of characters who witness supernatural events in Shakespeare remains within ordinary experience.
14. In Shakespeare, the marvellous belongs to the plot while the dialogue stays true to life.
15. Hamlet questions his father's ghost the way any son would question something so dreadful.
16. Macbeth broods on the witches' prophecy the way an ambitious man would brood on a promise of a crown.
